verdict.summary: The extraction remains correct and complete. The shared cron_map module preserves the single field expander and derived schedule map, now refuses malformed workflow and schedule shapes without silently dropping lanes, and carries non-vacuous hermetic and live-tree tests. ci-latency-alert binds the shared objects while adapting CronMapError into its existing AlarmError reporting contract; dispatch-tick-floor and regate-sweep point to the new owner, and every affected sparse checkout includes that owner. The module is enrolled in the self-test suite, required-file seams are updated, and the workflow comments consistently name the new source. I found no trust-check weakening, permissive fallback, workflow permission expansion, secret exposure, or reviewer-directed injection. Round 6 also had no findings, so the result is materially unchanged.
